description: Attack n=4096 B=2 — now the largest remaining geomean term (still routed to torch.geqrf ~52k us; all other shapes are fast). Brief 7 showed the BATCHED panel loses here because with only 2 matrices there is no batch concurrency. So optimize for a SINGLE large matrix instead: blocked Householder where each 4096x4096 matrix's trailing update (I-VT^TV^T)C is a LARGE TF32 tensor-core GEMM (loose ~1e-2 factor budget at n=4096 makes TF32, even FP16, comfortably safe), and the very tall 4096xNB panel is factored with row-parallelism across many CTAs / a thread-block cluster (the tall-panel cooperative technique from brief 9: split m rows across CTAs, cross-CTA reductions via DSMEM, cluster.sync). Add n=4096 to the custom path; keep all other n exactly as the parent. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Route n=4096 through brief-9 cooperative cluster panel (K=32 CTAs/matrix split the m=4096 rows, mhyb=1024 so cluster runs the panels with m>=1024) + whole-batch TF32 trailing GEMM. All n<=2048 tests PASS (no regression). n=4096 'upper' case (B=1, test 18) FAILS: H contains NaN/Inf. Upper-triangular input has degenerate (all-zero-below-diagonal) columns; the cluster kernel's nz==false branch produces NaN. n=4096 dense (test 5) status not captured in tail. Need to fix the degenerate-column handling in the cluster kernel.

Trial 1 (K=16, mhyb=1024): n=4096 B=2 33295us (1.57x over geqrf 52199), geomean 5147 (1.039x over parent 5346). nsys n=4096: panel DOMINATES (cluster 65.6% + single-CTA short-panel 13.1% = 79%), TF32 trailing GEMM only ~21%. Trial 2 (mhyb=256): more panels on cluster -> n=4096 32947us, geomean 5143. Cluster panel is the bottleneck to attack.

cb sweep (mhyb=256): 8->42494, 12->37724, 16->32947(best), 20->34600, 32->76734us. Confirmed cb=16 optimum for the cluster panel. Then cluster CTA threads 128->256: n=4096 32947->31423us, geomean 5123.14 (1.044x over parent 5346). ncu(K=16): cluster kernel is latency/sync-bound (achieved occ 6.25%, 1 active warp/sched, issued 0.13/cyc) -- only 2*K=32 CTAs on 148 SMs at B=2. Validates CLEAN (n=4096 dense + upper, all guards).

K-sweep (occupancy-bound at B=2): K=8->33444, K=12->32779, K=16->31423us (higher K wins -- opposite of brief 9's n=512/1024 where K=2/8 won; at B=2 under-occupancy dominates sync cost). threads-sweep: 256 best (128->32947, 256->31423, 512->35057). mhyb 256 best (128->31607, 256->31423, 1024->33295). FP16 trailing REGRESSES (contention-matched ~47.8k vs TF32 31.4k; .half casts of big C + lost fused baddbmm cost > FP16 GEMM win). NOTE: heavy cross-GPU contention this window inflated absolute numbers ~2.4x uniformly (shape0 184 vs 90, shape3 21228 vs 8749) -- relative comparisons hold; TF32 (trial 3, 5123 geomean) is the clean keeper.

KEEPER (revert trial-4 FP16 to TF32). Clean benchmark (uncontended GPU): n=4096 B=2 = 31448us (1.66x over geqrf 52199), geomean 5122.46us (1.044x over parent 5346, 25.6x over baseline 131187). All other 11 shapes match baseline exactly (no regression). Validates CLEAN (n=4096 dense scaled_factor 0.571, n=4096 upper residual=0, all 3 guards incl n=400 off-grid). Final nsys n=4096: panel_factor_cluster_kernel 66.6% (the bottleneck, latency/sync-bound at 6.25pct occupancy = only 2*K=32 CTAs at B=2), TF32 trailing GEMM ~29%, single-CTA short panels 2.5%.

NOT YET in the global best (4861us) -- this n=4096 path is ORTHOGONAL to the n<=2048/tiny-n/TF32-trailing wins, so it stacks cleanly via a COMBINE.

APPROACH (the brief's thesis confirmed): brief 7's BATCHED single-CTA panel LOST at n=4096 B=2 (60984us, 1.23x SLOWER than geqrf) because 2 matrices give only 2 CTAs. The fix = brief 9's COOPERATIVE CLUSTER panel: a thread-block cluster of K CTAs splits ONE matrix's tall m=4096 panel by rows, cross-CTA reductions via DSMEM (cluster.sync + map_shared_rank, sm_100a). At B=2 that's 2*K=32 CTAs (vs 2) -- turns idle SMs into row-parallel reduction throughput. Hybrid: cluster for tall panels (m>=mhyb=256), single-CTA panel for short. Whole-batch TF32 trailing GEMM (the 20*n*eps factor budget at n=4096 ~1.2e-2 is the loosest of any shape -- TF32 is comfortably safe for ALL conditioning; measured dense scaled 0.571, upper 0).

WHAT MOVED THE NUMBER (5 trials, all built/measured/committed): (1) cluster panel K=16 + TF32 trailing: 33295us (1.57x over geqrf) -- the win. (2) mhyb 1024->256 (more panels on cluster): 32947. (3) cluster CTA threads 128->256: 31423 (best) -- ncu showed the kernel latency/sync-bound at 6.25pct occupancy / 1 active warp-per-scheduler, so more warps/CTA hide the cluster.sync stalls. (4) FP16 trailing: REGRESSED (.half casts of the big C 4096x4080 + lost fused baddbmm_ epilogue cost more than 2x FP16 GEMM saves; trailing is only 29pct). (5) revert to TF32 = keeper.

FULLY SWEPT TO OPTIMA: K=16 (HARDWARE MAX cluster on this B200 -- K>=18 faults cudaErrorInvalidClusterSize even with NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed); threads=256 (128/256/512 -> 32947/31423/35057); cb=16 (8/12/16/20/32 -> 42494/37724/32947/34600/76734); mhyb=256 (128/256/1024 -> 31607/31423/33295). KEY FINDING: HIGHER K wins at B=2 (K=8/12/16 -> 33444/32779/31423us) -- OPPOSITE of brief 9's n=512/1024 (K=2/8 optimal) because at B=2 the under-occupancy is so extreme it dominates the per-column cluster.sync cost.

PROFILE (nsys+ncu, n=4096, saved at the keeper SHA): panel_factor_cluster_kernel 66.6pct (THE bottleneck), TF32 trailing GEMM ~29pct, single-CTA short panels 2.5pct. ncu on the cluster panel: achieved occupancy 6.25pct, 1.00 active warp/scheduler, 0.13 issued/cyc, 2.76pct SM throughput, 0.13pct DRAM -- catastrophically latency/sync-bound, purely because there are only 2*K=32 CTAs on 148 SMs (the HW cluster cap of 16 is the wall, NOT per-SM SMEM/registers). This is the dominant remaining cost.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not closed -- worth fresh briefs; the manager's call):
1. TSQR-HR PANEL (the structural unlock past the 32-CTA wall). I PROTOTYPED + VERIFIED the math in torch (recon err 3.8e-15, tau matches geqrf to 2e-16): factor row-blocks INDEPENDENTLY (G CTAs, G>>16, ZERO per-column cross-CTA sync -> fills the GPU at B=2), combine the R-blocks, reconstruct geqrf-exact (H,tau) via the DIRECT column-recurrence HR (NOT a 2nd geqrf, which would be circular). This is the ONLY structure that removes the per-column cluster.sync wall entirely. CAVEAT measured-on-paper: the HR reflector-apply is O(m*nb^2) m-length work, so net gain is uncertain -- but it converts the serial-sync panel into an embarrassingly-parallel local phase + a small combine. brief 1's CholeskyQR2+HR used no-pivot LU (blew up on ~4/60 matrices); the direct-recurrence HR I verified is stable. A dedicated macro brief.
2. COMBINE this n=4096 path onto the current global best (4861us) -- it is orthogonal and stacks cleanly (the best still routes n=4096 to geqrf). Expected ~ another few-pct geomean drop.
3. 2-level micro-panel inside the cluster (block-apply the IB reflectors to far cols as one rank-IB WY) -- my sync-count analysis suggests it ADDS cross-CTA syncs (Gram+W reductions) for the cluster, so likely neutral/negative on a latency-bound kernel, but unmeasured.
4. Trailing GEMM (29pct): many small late-panel GEMMs at B=2 (530+362 instances) are launch-bound; a fused/persistent trailing driver or CUDA-graph could cut launch overhead (overlaps brief 15's glue work).
NOTE: heavy cross-GPU contention hit this window intermittently (uniform ~2.4x inflation across ALL shapes, e.g. shape0 184 vs 90, shape3 21228 vs 8749 -- the same anomaly brief 9 logged); the keeper's 5122us was measured on a CLEAN uncontended GPU and re-confirmed (31448/31469 two clean runs).
